title: Dog antics and Kilmer's dog
summary: Stories of the dog in the wheelbarrow, dragging pots, and Kilmer's dog tearing up roses.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Don't think that dog can't run, that dog can do 90. Yeah. But he told me the other night when I hit him on his back, Look out! I said, uh-huh.
He looked out. He looked out.

Someone cut back there, got up with my wheelbarrow, man, back there, and got up in there, and I got the hood pipe and wet him up. I said, I'm wet the hood yard, man. I'm wet the hood yard. I'll make sure.

He told me one night, he said, his thing called him up. He said, that dog, he said, I'll build him a nice doghouse and put a foam rubber mattress in there. You know where that dog sleeps? In my wheelbarrow.
That's right. I'd rather go back in my wheelbarrow. So I take the wheelbars upside down now. I don't let him sleep in that no more. Does he go in his house?
He goes in his house now. He learns.

Soon the light come out in the morning, he come out of that house. My wife, he'll be right there. He'll get them pots. Yeah, he'll get them pots. And when he gets to eatin' with his pot, he take that pot and make more noise with three people back there. Drag that pot all around the yard, man. I'll be laying out. Yeah, he drag that pot out. So I take the pot now when I get to feed him and put it up on top of my ladder. You know, right at the top of the ladder, where he can't get it. But see, if I lay it, lay it down, he'll stay there and play that pot all day, drag it all over, you know. Break up all my flowers, I see. I think I'm going to brush you.
You got trouble with your animals, huh?

Yeah, you got trouble. He might be a good puppy, but he's giving me trouble now. My wife said, don't beat him. He's too cute. I say, yeah, you too cute. I say, I'm not cute, huh? Don't beat him, baby. He's too cute. He's too cute. Well, you shouldn't beat him too hard. Who? Tell him I get paper and light it and run it with that. I'm going to light it. Give me that stick over there.
You're supposed to hit him with, roll up the newspaper and get him with it.

No, no, I'm dog-hawty. He's too cute. Kilmer got a dog that tore his yard up so bad, he looked like a hog pet back there, man. You go back by Kilmer's house, man, done tore up all the grass and everything. And then he got all puddles of water, all the ground, all tore up. He had it nice back there. He used to go back there and help him to cut the grass back there, you know, sometimes, I had time. He had a dog that tore the whole yard up. All the rose bushes, beautiful rose bushes, American beauty roses. He done tore that all that up.
But he doesn't get beat up.

He had pink roses, yellow, and red roses. Beautiful roses. I mean roses grow that big. Oh, see? That dog done tore up all those rose bushes. And he got a house too to sleep in. Kilmer got him a house, but he don't sleep in that house, he's asleep on that lawn.
Kilmer got a drumstick for his dog. He's whipping. He's whipping. He saw him hit that big, he saw him on the side of his head. He weigh almost 100 pounds.
Yeah, Kilmer's dog was almost 100 pounds. What kind of dog? He's got a shepherd.
Oh, a shepherd. Well, tough guy's half shepherd and half collie.
